title: Tradition or eclectic?
hook: you might deepen one tradition or keep drawing from many, tagged and apart; Ruth and Orpah both choose honestly (Ruth 1)
tomorrow: after Pascal died, a servant found something sewn into his coat. what?

segments.voice: Yesterday's line: small and real. The widow's two coins outweighed the rich gifts. Today, a bigger question about the road itself.

Some friends grow up in one faith and go deeper. Some read everything and keep a little of each. Somebody always has an opinion about which is real. The book of Ruth begins at that kind of crossroads. Naomi, an Israelite woman living in Moab, has lost her husband and both her sons. She decides to go home to Bethlehem, and she tells her two Moabite daughters-in-law to go back to their mothers' houses. Orpah weeps, kisses her, and turns back. Ruth won't let go.
screen: `ONE FAITH, OR A LITTLE OF EACH?` → `NAOMI TURNS FOR HOME.` → `ORPAH KISSES HER AND GOES BACK.` → `RUTH WON'T LET GO.`

segments.voice: Ruth says: "whither thou goest, I will go; and where thou lodgest, I will lodge: thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God." So which daughter-in-law was right? Look closely, and the book never blames Orpah. Naomi herself told her to go, and she goes back, the text says, to her people and her gods, with a kiss. Ruth goes deep. She binds herself to one people and one God, and the book ends with her as great-grandmother of King David. Today's question: deepen one tradition, or keep drawing from many? This path's answer is that both can be honest. Ruth's way is a deep well, dug in one place. The way this path has walked all along is the other: many wells, each with its name on it, never poured together. What makes either honest is the same as in Ruth's story: you choose it with open eyes and love, not drift into it. Here's what this path shares with Judaism: a choice made with love and open eyes is honored. Jewish tradition honors Ruth's, and reads her book at the festival of Shavuot. And here's the honest difference. In Jewish tradition, Ruth's choice is a full joining, one people and one covenant. This path asks no one to join anything, and keeps each source whole instead.
screen: `THY PEOPLE SHALL BE MY PEOPLE.` · `THE BOOK NEVER BLAMES ORPAH.` · `ONE DEEP WELL, OR MANY NAMED ONES.` · `RUTH JOINS; THIS PATH JOINS NOTHING.` · then, large: `MY HONEST PATH.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes and set two pictures side by side: one well dug deep in a single place, and a road past many wells, each with its own name. Don't decide anything. Just notice which way you lean, the way a plant leans toward a window.
Tradition or eclectic: deepen one tradition, like Ruth, or keep drawing from many, tagged and apart. Both honest, if chosen with open eyes.
Here's the line: my honest path, chosen with open eyes, the way Ruth chose. Day 1595, done.

Ruth.meaning: a Moabite woman who chose Naomi's people and God

Moab.meaning: a land east of the Dead Sea, Ruth's homeland

Orpah.meaning: Naomi's other daughter-in-law, who went home

Shavuot.meaning: the Jewish festival of weeks, marking the giving of the Torah
